correctness.rationale: Finite generator uniquely defines an irreducible stationary law for a>0. Pair generator identities give exact correlations. Uniform polynomial generator convergence and compactness transfer stationary identities to all subsequential limits. The recurrences M_(k+1)=k M_(k-1)/((k+1)b²-1) and E[HX^k]=b M_(k+1) identify all compactly supported mixed moments. A rescaled symmetric beta marginal with the specified conditional hub sign has exactly these moments, hence uniquely identifies the limit. Script verifies finite stationary generators and several moments, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Exact stationary joint law and positive fixed-noise variance for growing stars are not asserted by inspected star mixing theorem or annealed complex-network results. General stationary-distribution results are narrower in observable/graph hypotheses and do not imply this beta limit. This is a qualified best-knowledge priority judgment, not a uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: A general exact stationary law for telegraph-driven linear flow with state-dependent switching might subsume the beta density, even if no noisy-voter star match is indexed.
A less accessible exact star-graph stationary calculation may derive the same law.
Published reduced-generator rates make the beta calculation mathematically accessible, and priority must be understood as specific explicit stationary finding, not discovery of the reduced model.

value.rationale: The hub controls a positive fraction of collective stationary fluctuations even at fixed noise as its number of leaves diverges. The explicit, non-Gaussian full beta law and hub-conditioned sign profile explain this lack of self-averaging and quantify it beyond routine finite moment evaluations; they distinguish singular hub networks from homogeneous mean-field noisy voting.
